clue.text: Fond about boozer lacking form?

indicators.note: the fond word goes about, that is around, the boozer's letters

parts.note: fond of someone means amorous
PH, public house, is a pub or boozer

explanation.surface: Someone fond of the pub has let themselves go and lost their figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shapeless or without definite structure is described as amorphous, literally 'without shape' in Greek.

clue.text: Government partly includes having to read minutes

indicators.note: the words 'read minutes' include the answer inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: Part of a government's routine involves having to read the minutes of meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to' is just a link; 'partly' marks the definition as a shortened word, since the answer is a clipped form of administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for administration, which can mean the government of the day, so a clipped word fits 'partly'.

clue.text: Aim for the thing Gordius has?

parts.note: a thing is an object
the setter Gordius speaking of himself would say I have, contracted to I'VE

explanation.surface: A question about what goal the setter has in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name; read 'Gordius has' as 'I've'.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective is a goal, target or aim one works towards.

clue.text: Claiming to make the sound of a hooter or small bell?

indicators.note: imitating the noises named tells us to say a phrase aloud and hear another word

parts.note: a car hooter goes PARP and a little bell goes TING, so the phrase is 'parp or ting'

explanation.surface: Someone claims to imitate a horn or a tinkling bell.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a British accent, with no R sounded, 'parp or ting' comes out close to the definition's word; a hooter is a British name for a car horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Purporting to be something is professing or claiming to be it, often falsely.

clue.text: It's atrocious to urge a revolt

indicators.note: to revolt is to turn over, so the letters of 'to urge a' are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: Urging people to rise up is called a shocking thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is an atrocious act, a deed so shocking it causes public anger.

clue.text: Hitler's bodyguard held rigorous bodily pleasures

indicators.note: the bodyguard's letters hold the rigorous word between them

parts.note: the SS (Schutzstaffel) began as Hitler's personal guard
rigorous, precise, means exact

explanation.surface: A Nazi guard reportedly kept physical pleasures under strict control.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of intercourse are physical, carnal pleasures of the body.

clue.text: Important person died after arrest

indicators.note: the word for died comes after the word for arrest

parts.note: to nab is to arrest or catch
OB is short for Latin obiit, he or she died

explanation.surface: A notable figure died soon after being arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a wealthy, important person, originally a returned rich official from India.

clue.text: Lacking cover, but not altogether underdressed

indicators.note: dressed in the sense of arranged or put in order, so these letters are rearranged
not the whole word, so the final letter of 'under' is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone underdressed is not quite naked, but nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'underdressed' into 'under' and 'dressed': 'not altogether' trims 'under' to UNDE, and 'dressed' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naked means having no clothes or covering at all.

clue.text: Put up with nothing short of Asian island

indicators.note: lacking, so the island's name loses the letter for nothing

parts.note: Borneo is a large island in Southeast Asia
O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: A traveller will tolerate nothing less than a trip to an Asian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Something borne has been endured or tolerated, the past participle of bear.

clue.text: Male that might be 19 across

parts.note: a man who could be engaged, that is betrothed, to someone

explanation.surface: A man who might be committed to a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart or male partner is someone a woman may become engaged to.

clue.text: One-time premier rank

definitions.meaning: John ... was UK Prime Minister from 1990 to 1997
a military officer grade above captain

explanation.definitionFit: Names both a former British Prime Minister and an army officer's rank.

clue.text: Cab turned colour — setter's getting stuffed

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: turned back, so the colour word is read in reverse

parts.note: red is a colour
the setter's means 'my', as the setter speaks of himself

explanation.surface: A taxi changed colour while the setter's vehicle was being stuffed.
explanation.definitionFit: The craft of preparing and mounting animal skins, so the creatures end up stuffed.

clue.text: Girl keeps city memory of bringing back past characters

indicators.note: the girl's name keeps the other letters inside it

parts.note: Nancy is a girl's name
EC is the postcode area for the City of London
ROM is read-only memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A girl holds onto a memory of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing back past characters' means summoning the dead, not reviving old letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The black art of summoning the spirits of the dead to foretell the future.

clue.text: It must be 19 across to work and 6 down is without it

definitions.text: It must be 19 across to work and 6 down is without it

parts.words: It must be 19 across to work and 6 down is without it
parts.note: a car's transmission must be engaged to drive, and someone naked has no clothes, or kit

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that must be committed to function and that the naked lack.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a car's transmission setting and clothing or equipment.

clue.text: One to call boss?

parts.note: read as one who rings, a ringer, plus a leader, the boss of a gang

explanation.surface: A question about whom to address as boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The instigator who leads a group, especially in wrongdoing, is its boss figure.

clue.text: When across the street it may need to be wet

definitions.text: it may need to be wet

indicators.note: the word for when lies across, that is around, the street's letters

parts.note: while means when, during the time that

explanation.surface: Something needing to be moistened when crossing the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet your whistle' is an idiom for having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To wet one's whistle is to take a drink, so this thing may need to be moistened.

clue.text: At which point turned up here and now?

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters of 'up here' and 'now' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about when someone turned up in the present place.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal adverb meaning immediately after which, at which point in events.

clue.text: Faculty of moral sense lacking study?

indicators.note: without, so the word for study is removed

parts.note: conscience is one's moral sense
to con is to study or learn

explanation.surface: A university department is accused of having no moral sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty in the sense of a field of knowledge or a university department.

clue.text: Cavalier heard with blunt weapon at social centre

indicators.note: said aloud, so the word for cavalier is heard as another

parts.note: a cavalier is a mounted soldier, a knight
a club is a blunt weapon

explanation.surface: A mounted soldier was heard with a cudgel at a social gathering place.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue for drinking and dancing at night is a social venue.

clue.text: English learnt to translate, but not in time

indicators.note: translating changes the form, so the letters of 'learnt' are reworked

explanation.surface: English is learnt in order to translate, but not on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting exists outside of time.

clue.text: Alfalfa's fortune curtailed by an eagle

definitions.note: read as 'alfalfa is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: cut off at the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: luck is fortune
an erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: An alfalfa farmer's luck has been cut short by a bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for alfalfa, the clover-like fodder plant.

clue.text: Committed to complete wearing a glove

indicators.note: the word for complete wears, so surrounds, the glove

parts.note: to end is to complete
a gage is a glove thrown down as a challenge

explanation.surface: Someone is determined to finish wearing a glove.
explanation.definitionFit: Committed to marry, or busy and occupied, as engaged means.

clue.text: Impressive story editor started to edit as a funeral ode

parts.note: an epic is a grand narrative

indicators.note: started means the beginning, so the first letter of edit

explanation.surface: An editor begins revising a grand tale as a funeral poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge or elegy sung at a burial is a funeral poem.

clue.text: Direction to top brute …

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a beast is a brute

explanation.surface: An order to kill a brutal creature.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four cardinal compass points.

clue.text: Told to watch one's step?

indicators.note: told means spoken aloud, so the word for watch is heard as another

parts.note: to stare is to watch fixedly

explanation.surface: Someone is warned to be careful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch one's step' is a warning to be careful; 'one's' is just a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step in a staircase.

clue.text: … in opposite region

parts.note: carrying on from the previous clue, the region opposite the east, that is the west

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: something lying in the opposite region.
explanation.definitionFit: Western, belonging to the part of the world opposite the Orient.

clue.text: Partly full, it retains a quantity of liquid

indicators.note: only part of the words 'full, it retains' is used, a run spanning them

explanation.surface: A vessel that is partly full still retains some liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of liquid volume.

clue.text: 5 years old, about to become a star!

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: turned about, so the word for years is reversed

parts.note: age is how many years old one is

explanation.surface: A five-year-old is about to become a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Growth of scheme to be French and English

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
être is French for to be

explanation.surface: Development of a scheme to be both French and English.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree, here the large deciduous tree common in London streets, is a growth.

clue.text: Dutch leader left crumbling city

indicators.note: the leader of Dutch is its first letter
crumbling breaks the word left apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A Dutch leader departed from a decaying city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is a Dutch city famous for its blue-and-white pottery.

clue.text: She's not quite like other women

definitions.note: a woman's name; the 's is read as 'is', a link

indicators.note: not complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: being like others means normal

explanation.surface: A woman described as somewhat different from others.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as in Bellini's opera heroine.

clue.text: River shellfish the European finds very poor indeed

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
a crab is a shellfish
le is 'the' in French, a European language

explanation.surface: A diner from Europe finds the river shellfish dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means extremely bad, abominable.
